conviction_note: Q3 is not pre-released and the release also carries the first Dalata pro forma figures and the Q4 booking read, so the move is sized near the 7% new-numbers base and close to this name's own recent print reactions (-8.5%, -3.6%, -6.8%). The direction is close to a coin: Scandic's landlord Pandox (comparable lease RevPAR +6%, occupancy 77 vs 75, Sweden strongest) and Swedish August hotel data (room revenue +12%) point to a Q3 above management's own 'flat occupancy, higher rates' guide. Against that, the stock is up 25.8% in 60 days and trades above the 100 SEK average target, and it fell after each of its last three prints. p_up 52 on a sum of findings of +0.1; the two measurements agree in being near zero.

already_public.what: Q2 2026 report: management expects a good Q3, with occupancy in line with last year and higher average room rates (qualitative, no numbers).
Dalata hotel operations acquisition completed for EUR 500m cash and debt free, consolidated in 'Other Europe' from 2026-11-02. Pro forma figures deferred to the Q3 report.

Pandox Q3 2026 (landlord with revenue-based leases, 48 Scandic hotels / 10,898 rooms): comparable lease revenue +7%, RevPAR +6%, occupancy ~77% (75), ADR +4%, strongest growth in Sweden. Dalata portfolio revenue +4% UK, +1% Ireland.
Broker target raises in October: DNB Carnegie 108->112 (Oct 12), UBS 103->109 (Oct 15), Morgan Stanley 74->80 (Oct 2); 4-month average target 100.33 SEK.

new_in_release.expect: Q3 revenue, RevPAR and adjusted EBITDA against Q3 2025's 6,372 MSEK / RevPAR 966 / adj. EBITDA 1,088 MSEK. Counterparty and market data point to RevPAR growth of mid-single digits and a modest beat on the company's own guide. Up, modestly.

First pro forma financials for the Dalata operations (57 hotels, ~12,500 rooms), plus post-deal leverage. Pandox's figures show soft Dalata top-line growth (Ireland +1%). Direction unknown, possibly slightly negative.
Qualitative Q4 booking situation. Pandox flags a strong Q4 comparison and market outlook 'stable'. Unknown. Possible new financial targets for the combined group, not sourced as scheduled.
Q3 free cash flow plus the first post-deal leverage (EUR 500m funded from cash and facilities; net debt/adj. EBITDA was 0.1x at Q2). Leverage rises by construction. Unknown how it is received.
No change expected; the semi-annual instalment went ex around 2026-11-06.

findings.finding: Q3 demand looks to have run above Scandic's own guide of flat occupancy and higher rates. Its landlord Pandox, whose leases are revenue-based and include 48 Scandic hotels, reported comparable lease RevPAR +6%, occupancy about 77% (75) and ADR +4% for Q3, with Sweden the strongest market. Swedish market data for August showed room revenue +12% and prices about +9%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 missed the Infront adj. EBITDA bar (796 vs 825 MSEK) and the stock fell 6.76% on 2026-07-15. Q3 2025 was in line (1,088 vs 1,089) and moved -0.85% on 2025-10-29. The three most recent print days all fell (2026-02-18 -8.47%, 2026-04-22 -3.56%, 2026-07-15 -6.76%; the first two dates are inferred from volume spikes, not confirmed against the release).
findings.original_quote: Independent series (sv, Dagens PS citing Visita/Benchmarking Alliance, 2026-09-03): 'Samtidigt steg hotellens logiintäkter med hela 12 procent.' / 'Snittpriserna ökade med omkring 9 procent både i storstäderna och ute i landet.' (Room revenue rose 12% in August; average prices rose about 9% in the big cities and the rest of the country.) Company guide: 'Beläggningsgraden bedöms därför bli i nivå med föregående år, samtidigt som genomsnittliga rumspriser väntas bli högre.'
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced. The stock rose from about 88 to 106.9 SEK between late September and 2026-11-09, and DNB Carnegie and UBS raised targets on Oct 12 and 15, after the summer market data came out. What is left is the gap between the company's flat-occupancy guide, which is still the anchor for any estimate built off the Q2 call, and Pandox's +2 points of occupancy. If that were fully priced, a guide-level print would sell off, and the stock fell 2% on Pandox's own report day (2026-10-22). Sized small because the bar is unsourced and the readthrough is a counterparty proxy, not Scandic's own number. Net of the rest of the company: Finland was guided only 'broadly in line', and SEK translation can dilute reported growth.
findings.independence: Swedish market series from Visita/Benchmarking Alliance via Dagens PS (https://www.dagensps.se/weekend/rekordsommar-for-svenska-hotell-men-sverige-ar-fortfarande-en-turistdvarg/, 2026-09-03), and Tillväxtverket summer hotel guest nights +5.6% (https://www.placera.se/telegram/svensk-turism-slog-sommarrekord-20260929). Pandox's market chart also uses Benchmarking Alliance data, so the two are partly the same series.

findings.finding: The Dalata operations Scandic now consolidates grew slowly in Q3. On Pandox's revenue-based leases, Dalata portfolio revenue grew an estimated 4% in the UK and 1% in Ireland, against a strong 2025 Irish summer. The first pro forma disclosure in this release will show a lower-growth addition of about 12,500 rooms, alongside higher leverage from the EUR 500m price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No precedent: this is the first pro forma disclosure. The 2025-10-30 session (+6.26%, the day after the Q3 2025 report, which carried a Dalata acquisition update) is the closest analogue, and its cause is not confirmed.
findings.why_not_priced: Pandox published the figure, but it is buried in a property company's report and framed as 'well in line with our expectations'. Scandic's CEO told the market in July that Dalata was 'growing faster than the market'. If the market had read the +1% Ireland figure, the run-up into the deal's completion (+2.42% on 2026-11-02) would be harder to explain. Small, because Pandox calls the development on plan and the deal was priced at about 6x 2024 adjusted EBITDA.
findings.independence: CEO claim in the other direction (Placera/Direkt, 2026-07-15, https://www.placera.se/telegram/scandic-hotels-bra-start-pa-3-kv-vd-20260715). Nothing independent supports the weaker read.

findings.finding: The stock goes into the print at 106.9 SEK, above the 100.33 SEK four-month average target and above two of the three October targets. That follows +25.8% in 60 days and +11.25% in 20 days, so a good Q3 is the expectation and the threshold for a positive reaction is raised. On its last three prints the stock fell 3.6-8.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 (2026-02-18, -8.47%): RevPAR beat but profit and dividend came in slightly below expectations. Q2 2026 (2026-07-15, -6.76%): a miss. The name sells mixed or in-line prints.

findings.why_not_priced: This is itself a statement about what is priced: the run-up is the market having already bought the strong summer. It is filed as a small negative only because the short register (2.69%, unchanged) shows no crowded short to squeeze, so an in-line print has no positioning fuel.

baseline_tension: The priced lean is +1.05 (mostly the short-squeeze component on a modest 2.69% short) and the 20- and 60-day run-ups are +11% and +26%. The fundamental evidence agrees with the lean on the number, but the run-up suggests the good summer is already bought, so the findings net to about zero and p_up sits just above 50.
language_note: Scandic's own release, invitation and Q2 outlook are published in both Swedish and English; the Swedish Q2 report adds nothing the English one lacks beyond the original wording of the guide.

Swedish press carried the independent market series the English sources did not: the Visita/Benchmarking Alliance August data (room revenue +12%, prices about +9%) via Dagens PS, and Tillväxtverket's summer hotel guest nights +5.6% via Placera/Finwire.
